questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and well labelled diagram of an insect pollinated flower. *(6 marks)*
Distinguish between pollination and fertilization. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Pollination | Fertilization |
|---|---|
| The **transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma** of a flower. | The **fusion of the male gamete (nucleus from the pollen tube) with the female gamete (egg cell) in the ovule** to form a zygote. |
| It takes place **before** fertilization, outside the ovule, on the stigma. | It takes place **after** pollination, inside the ovule in the ovary. |
| It needs an agent: insects, wind, water or animals. | It needs no external agent; the pollen grain grows a **pollen tube** down the style to the ovule. |
| It may be **self-pollination** or **cross-pollination**. | It produces a **zygote**, which develops into the embryo. |
| It does not produce a seed or fruit. | The ovule becomes the **seed** and the ovary becomes the **fruit**. |

Thus pollination only brings the pollen to the stigma, whereas fertilization is the actual joining of the gametes.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How is the

(i) Coconut fruit

(ii) Cotton seed

(iii) Mango fruit

adapted to their various method of dispersal? *(3, 3, 3 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Coconut fruit - dispersal by water.** The thick **fibrous husk (mesocarp)** contains many air spaces, so the fruit is **light and floats**; the smooth **waterproof outer skin (exocarp)** keeps water out, and the hard shell protects the seed. It is carried by rivers and sea currents to far shores, where it germinates.

(ii) **Cotton seed - dispersal by wind.** The seed is covered with **long, light, silky hairs (cotton fibres)** that give a large surface area in proportion to its mass, so that it is **carried far by the wind**.

(iii) **Mango fruit - dispersal by animals.** The fruit has a **fleshy, sweet, juicy and often brightly coloured mesocarp**, which attracts animals (birds, bats, monkeys, man) to eat it. The seed inside is protected by a **hard stony endocarp**, so it is thrown away or passes through the gut unharmed and is dropped at a distance from the parent plant.
